task: A simulation of LRU, LFU and ARC on the given trace with capacity 5: hits, misses, hit rates, the cache state after each access, and which policy wins and why.

criteria.text: LRU: 9 hits and 21 misses out of 30 (hit rate 30%).
LFU: 12 hits and 18 misses (40%), with its tie-breaking rule stated. 12 holds for LRU, FIFO or smallest-id tie-breaking, with or without retained frequency history.
ARC simulated with its four lists (T1, T2, B1, B2) and the adaptive target p: 12 hits and 18 misses (40%).
Shows the cache state after each access for each policy (a table or list of 30 steps per policy).

The conclusion matches the counts (LFU and ARC tie at 12 and both beat LRU at 9), explained by the frequently re-referenced items (1, 2, 3) being evicted by LRU during the runs of one-off items, while frequency (LFU) and the frequency list T2 (ARC) protect them.

reference: Trace of 30 accesses. Reference counts from two independent implementations: LRU 9/30; LFU 12/30 under every common tie-break; ARC (Megiddo-Modha) 12/30.
